summary: Iraq has ended visa on arrival: visitors now need an e-Visa before they travel (USD 160 per the UK FCDO; Iraq's portal says it is valid 30 days, the FCDO says 60), or an embassy visa. The Kurdistan Region issues its own e-Visa, online or on arrival for many nationalities, valid only inside the Kurdistan Region.

passportValidity.text: Your passport must be valid for at least 6 months on arrival in Iraq.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Iraq entry requirements

travelInsurance.text: No official source we could find states whether travel insurance is required to enter Iraq. Many policies exclude Iraq, so check that yours covers it, including medical evacuation.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Iraq

onwardTicket.text: Have a return ticket, or a ticket out of Iraq to a third country, before you fly: without one, airlines may refuse boarding, according to UK government travel advice. No Iraqi official source we could find states the rule.

source.name: UK FCDO travel advice — Iraq entry requirements

proofOfFunds.text: No official source we could find states a funds requirement or amount for visitors to Iraq. Cards are of little use, so carry enough US dollars in cash for your stay.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Iraq

currencyLimits.text: On arrival and departure you must declare foreign currency or items worth more than USD 10,000 (or the equivalent), and Iraqi dinars over IQD 200,000.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Iraq entry requirements

notes: Photography near checkpoints, government buildings and military sites is dangerous — always ask before photographing people or infrastructure.
Drones are effectively prohibited and will be confiscated.
Evidence of travel to Israel can lead to refusal of entry.

payments.text: Iraq is overwhelmingly cash-based. Bring US dollars (newer, undamaged notes) to exchange. Cards work only at a handful of upmarket hotels, and ATMs accepting foreign cards are scarce, though somewhat better in Erbil.

safety.text: The FCDO advises against all travel to large parts of Iraq — including Kirkuk, Ninawa and Salah al-Din provinces, western Anbar and Sadr City — and against all but essential travel to the rest, including Baghdad and the Kurdistan Region. It reports Iranian strikes in Iraq, including the Kurdistan Region, since 8 July 2026. Terrorism, kidnapping and sudden unrest remain real risks; if you go, travel with an experienced local operator.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Iraq travel advice

bestTimeToVisit.text: Spring (March–April) and fall (October–November) avoid the ferocious summer, when temperatures can pass 50°C in Baghdad and the south.

idp.text: Iraq is a party to the 1968 Vienna Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1949 Geneva one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1968 Vienna version. A permit issued under the 1949 Geneva Convention carries no treaty obligation here.

driving.text: Iraq is a party to the 1968 Vienna Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1949 Geneva one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1968 Vienna version. A permit issued under the 1949 Geneva Convention carries no treaty obligation here. Whether a permit is required in addition to a national license, and for how long a foreign license may be used, are set by national road law and have not been checked for Iraq yet.

tips.text: The Kurdistan Region (Erbil, Sulaymaniyah) issues its own e-Visa, online or on arrival for many nationalities, but it is valid in the Kurdistan Region ONLY. Travelling from Erbil to Baghdad or Mosul requires a federal Iraqi e-Visa; decide which you need before you fly.
Bring your budget in US dollars cash, in good condition — older or marked notes are refused. The e-Visa itself is paid online when you apply, not in cash at the airport.
Expect frequent checkpoints between cities. Carry your passport at all times, keep visa copies on your phone, and build waiting time into any road journey.
During Ashura and the Arbaeen pilgrimage, Karbala and Najaf receive millions of visitors — accommodation sells out and roads close. Dress conservatively at all religious sites year-round.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Iraq?
faq.answer: Yes. Iraq no longer issues visit visas on arrival: the UK, Canadian and Australian governments all say you must get a visa before you travel, usually the e-Visa on Iraq's official portal (evisa.iq). The FCDO gives the fee as USD 160 and the validity as 60 days; Iraq's portal says 30 days, so plan on 30. Apply at least 24 hours before departure — airlines check for the visa before boarding. Nationalities not eligible for the e-Visa apply at an Iraqi embassy. The exception is Iran: under a bilateral agreement, Iranian citizens arriving by air can enter without a visa.

faq.question: Is a visa for the Kurdistan Region the same as an Iraqi visa?
faq.answer: No. The Kurdistan Regional Government issues its own e-Visa (visit.gov.krd), valid only inside the Kurdistan Region. Its portal says citizens of its 'Country List A' can get it online or on arrival at any KRI entry point, while others need a sponsor in the Region; the fee is IQD 100,000, the visa is valid 90 days from issue and allows a 30-day stay. To travel on to Baghdad or anywhere else in federal Iraq you need a separate Iraqi e-Visa.

faq.question: Is Iraq safe for tourists?
faq.answer: Iraq remains a high-risk destination: most governments advise against all travel, or against all nonessential travel because of terrorism, kidnapping and unrest. That said, organized tourism to Baghdad, Babylon, the southern shrine cities and especially the Kurdistan Region has grown since 2021. Go with an experienced operator, expect checkpoints, and follow advisories.

faq.question: Can Israeli citizens visit Iraq?
faq.answer: No. Israeli passport holders are not admitted to Iraq, and Iraqi law criminalises contact that would normalise relations. Evidence of travel to Israel in another passport can also cause problems at the border.

faq.question: How do I apply and pay for the Iraqi e-Visa?
faq.answer: Online, on Iraq's e-Visa portal (evisa.iq), with a valid passport and a digital photo on a white background; the fee is paid by secure online payment and the visa arrives by email to print and show at the border. The FCDO gives the fee as USD 160. Apply at least 24 hours before you fly and carry a return or onward ticket, or the airline may refuse boarding.
